Development And Operation Of Strategic Water Storage Tanks – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of a strategic potable water storage system to ensure reliable and sustainable water supply and support AlUla’s economic and tourism growth and future development needs. The project includes the development and operation of five strategic water storage tanks with a combined capacity of 295,000 m³, providing approximately 3 to 4 days of potable water reserves, alongside pumping stations, connection networks, and supporting infrastructure serving urban districts, heritage sites, the airport, and new development areas. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with a concession period of approximately 15 years, comprising 2 to 3 years of construction and 12 to 13 years of operations and maintenance, supported by availability-based payments linked to performance and water quality. The RFP is expected to be launched in Q4 2027, with phased completion targeted by 2031.

Enhancement And Operation Of Wastewater Treatment Plants – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the rehabilitation and expansion of the Wastewater Treatment Plant to increase treatment capacity, support economic growth, and enhance environmental sustainability. The project includes the rehabilitation of the existing plant with a capacity of 8,000 m³/day and its expansion using Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR) technology in two phases, adding 18,000 m³/day in Phase I and 36,000 m³/day in Phase II, bringing the total treatment capacity to 62,000 m³/day, alongside treated wastewater storage and pumping facilities, control systems, and supporting infrastructure. The project is planned to be delivered under a Build–Own–Operate–Transfer (BOOT) model, with a concession period of approximately 26 years, comprising 3 years of construction and rehabilitation and 23 years of operations, supported by capacity, output, and supplemental payments. The RFP is expected to be launched in Q2 2027.

Development And Operation Of A Solid Waste Management System – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of an integrated solid waste management system in AlUla to enhance environmental sustainability, increase recycling rates, and support a sustainable economy. The project includes the development of a Resource Management Park and a waste transfer station with a capacity of 76,000 tonnes annually, recycling facilities with a capacity of 45,000 tonnes annually, organic waste treatment facilities, construction and demolition waste processing facilities with a capacity of 220,000 tonnes annually, and engineered landfill cells with a total capacity of 5 million cubic metres, alongside supporting infrastructure. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with a concession period of 30 years, comprising 3 years of construction and 27 years of operations, supported by performance-based payments and waste gate and transfer fees. The RFP is planned to be launched in Q2 2027.

#RCU-OPP-000258
Learn More
Expansion Of Secondary Roads– PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of the secondary road network to enhance connectivity, support economic and tourism growth in AlUla, and facilitate access to new development areas, heritage sites, and nature reserves. The project covers the development of 18 secondary road and utility corridors totalling approximately 1,400 km, including new road construction and integrated infrastructure for water supply, electricity, telecommunications, street lighting, and stormwater drainage. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with an availability-based payment mechanism and a concession period of approximately 20 years. Operations and maintenance will cover roads only, with utilities handed over to the relevant entities. The RFP process for the project packages is planned to commence in early 2028, with phased completion targeted by 2033.

#RCU-OPP-000257
Learn More
Expansion Of Highways And Primary Roads – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development and upgrade of the primary road network to enhance connectivity and support economic and tourism growth in AlUla. The project covers the development and upgrade of five primary roads and associated utility networks, totalling 204 km, including new road construction, rehabilitation, cycling paths, and traffic-calming measures, alongside integrated water, electricity, telecommunications, and stormwater drainage infrastructure. The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with an availability-based payment mechanism and a concession period of 15 years. Operations and maintenance will cover roads only, with utilities handed over to the relevant entities. The RFP process for the project packages is planned to commence in early 2028, with phased completion targeted by 2032.

#RCU-OPP-000256
Learn More
AlUla International Airport Expansion – PPP Investment Opportunity
Active
Logistics & Industrial
Primary & Secondary Infrastructure

In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the expansion of AlUla International Airport to support economic and tourism growth and enhance AlUla’s air connectivity. The project includes a new passenger terminal of approximately 30,000 sqm, with a capacity of up to 3 million passengers annually, a 5,000 sqm cargo terminal incorporating world-class equestrian facilities, a private aviation terminal of approximately 10,000 sqm, general aviation and helicopter facilities, and an extension of the runway to 3,000 metres, in addition to roads, parking, maintenance facilities, utilities, and fuel facilities. Approximately 1 million sqm of land is also available for complementary commercial uses, including logistics, retail, hospitality, and aviation services. The project is planned to be delivered under a Build–Transfer–Operate (BTO) model, with a concession period of up to 35 years The RFP is expected to be launched in Q3 2027, with project completion targeted by 2032
